analysis.title: Europe Open - Aftermath
key_insights: US bonds sold off Tuesday after Fed's Waller said a 50bp hike is possible and a hot CPI print plus more Fedspeak (Logan, Goolsbee, Paulson) pointed to further tightening. The selloff spilled into Asia, with JGBs down 10bp.
Waller put a 50bp hike on the table if core inflation printed at 0.2%. Core came in at an unrounded 0.296% MoM.

Logan said it would make sense to pause after two more increases. Goolsbee called the October CPI report 'borderline disturbing'. Paulson still supported gradual tightening, citing limited wage pressures and inflation expectations consistent with the 2% target.
Dec OIS pricing stands at +28.5bp, with PPI due Thursday.

Citi's David Bieber says USTs have moved tactically long with risks concentrated close to current prices but remain structurally short. The bias is to higher yields, with next support at 106-00 / 107-00 in 10y TYs.
US equity futures rallied, with Nasdaq up 1.5%, helped by strong CoreWeave revenue guidance. US stocks closed slightly negative on Tuesday after choppy trading post CPI.

Citi's Regime Model moves equities to neutral, with the US the largest underweight and duration overweight via JGBs and Gilts. Systematic strategies are positive YTD, with carry and value offsetting trend-following losses.
The USD rally holds, with leveraged USD buying in flows. Asia-session interbank volumes were 21% below 30-day averages.
Citi likes owning AUD and NZD front-end skews, with 1m 25d RR at 1.25v for USD call. The Asia trader remains short AUD against USD and JPY.
Citi expects Dec FOMC implied event jump premium to trade in demand at about 50bp.
Trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine talks continued for a second day, with Ukraine calling them constructive. An Iran-reported tanker fire east of Hormuz highlights two-sided risks to the bearish oil case.
South Korea 10-day exports rose 111.9% YoY with imports at 45%. KRW was the top overnight performer, reaching 1333 vs USD.
BRL fell 1.26% Tuesday on dovish BCB minutes. BRL typically underperforms in Nov/Dec.
